title: Tri-SDK session-hint + shrinkwrap stream ergonomics; stabilize backoff windows
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: We observed subtle reconnect thundering and token refresh contention in mixed-language clients under bursty traffic. This PR introduces a lightweight cross-SDK "session-hint" to allow callers to signal session affinity windows, plus a shrinkwrap mechanism for stream consumer ergonomics so SDKs expose consistent, minimal surface area across Python, TypeScript, and Go. The goal is to make backoff behavior more predictable during credential swaps and to make stream consumption patterns easier to reason about for application authors.

What this PR does (high level):
- Add `session_hint` metadata to SDK connect operations (py/ts/go). This is an optional opaque string passed through transport and logged in credential telemetry to correlate session lifecycle events.
- Stabilize backoff windows by introducing an adaptive cap computed from session_hint entropy and recent failure rate; reduces thundering retries when many clients reconnect simultaneously.
- Add a shrinkwrap stream facade: small, explicit API surface for pull-streams with a single `next()`/`close()` pair (async iterator wrapper for Python/TS, channel-style consumer for Go). This reduces differences across SDKs and simplifies coroutine/Promise/Go-routine usage.
- Credential telemetry: emit lightweight events (session_hint, refresh_start, refresh_ok, refresh_fail, stale_cache_hit) so ops can measure credential churn without logging secrets. Telemetry is opt-out and uses existing metrics hooks.
- Version bumps for SDK packages to align with new API: py 0.17.2, ts 2.4.0, go 1.9.3.

Backend changes and compatibility notes:
- No server-side schema change required; session_hint is treated as free-form metadata by the control plane but is surfaced in logs and metrics.
- Existing clients will keep working; session_hint is optional. The shrinkwrap facade coexists with the richer stream API for now but is intended as the recommended path.

Testing and verification:
- Unit tests added for all three SDKs covering session_hint propagation, adaptive backoff calculation, and shrinkwrap iterator semantics.
- End-to-end integration test added to the CI matrix that spins up a local dev control plane, exercises credential rotation under concurrent reconnects (100 clients), and asserts tail latency and retry counts remain within the expected envelope.
- Loadbench: a small benchmark run showed a 28% reduction in simultaneous refresh attempts (peak) and a 6% improvement in 95th percentile token roundtrip during reconnection storms.

Checklist:
- [x] SDK API changes documented in CHANGES.md for each SDK
- [x] Integration tests added and green in CI (required flake fix applied)
- [x] Release notes drafted
- [x] No secret material included in telemetry payloads

Follow-ups (separate PRs):
- Optional: promote shrinkwrap facade to default in the next major SDK bump (requires deprecation cycle).
- Observability: add a dashboard panel for "session_hint churn" and a regression alert.

Notes on approach and rationale: The session_hint is intentionally minimal and opt-in; it gives platform and application owners a way to correlate client behavior to session lifecycles (for example, warmup phases, sticky routing, or short-lived workers). Shrinkwrap stream ergonomics were created after iterating on several in-house apps where small differences between async iterators, event emitters, and channel consumers caused production puzzles. By providing a predictable minimal shape we reduce accidental misuse and make cross-team onboarding easier.
